_description: Structural patterns that make text detectable as AI-generated. Each pattern includes a description, bad example, and fix.

patterns.name: triple_adjective_opener
patterns.description: Three adjectives stacked before a noun or in a list. AI defaults to groups of three.
patterns.example_bad: A comprehensive, innovative, and scalable solution
patterns.fix: Pick one specific adjective or replace with a concrete detail. 'A solution that handles 10K concurrent users' beats three vague adjectives.

patterns.name: mirror_paragraphs
patterns.description: Every paragraph follows the same intro-points-summary structure with similar length.
patterns.example_bad: X is important. It has A, B, and C. Therefore X matters. [repeat exact shape]
patterns.fix: Vary paragraph shapes. Some should be one sentence. Some six. Start one with a question. Let the content dictate the shape.

patterns.name: hedging_chains
patterns.description: Multiple qualifiers stacked in one sentence or across consecutive sentences.
patterns.example_bad: While it could potentially possibly help to some extent...
patterns.fix: Commit to a position. One qualifier max. 'It helps' or 'It might help' — not both.

patterns.name: parallel_lists
patterns.description: Every list item follows identical grammatical structure, forced into perfect parallelism.
patterns.example_bad: First, innovation matters. Second, efficiency matters. Third, quality matters.
patterns.fix: Break the pattern. Use different sentence shapes for each item. Real lists are messy.

patterns.name: uniform_sentence_length
patterns.description: All sentences fall between 15-25 words with minimal variation. Human std dev is 8-12 words; AI is 2-3.
patterns.example_bad: The platform offers comprehensive analytics. Users can track their performance metrics. The dashboard provides real-time insights.
patterns.fix: Mix dramatically. Follow a 4-word sentence with a 35-word one. Fragments count. 'Works great.' is a valid sentence.

patterns.name: em_dash_overuse
patterns.description: Excessive em dashes for parenthetical asides — often multiple per paragraph — creating a choppy rhythm.
patterns.example_bad: The solution — which was innovative — transformed the industry — creating new opportunities.
patterns.fix: One em dash per paragraph max. Use commas, periods, or parentheses for the rest.

patterns.name: synonym_cycling
patterns.description: Rotating synonyms for the same concept instead of repeating the clearest word.
patterns.example_bad: The platform... the solution... the tool... the system... the application...
patterns.fix: Pick the best word and repeat it. Repetition is natural. Cycling synonyms is not.

patterns.name: rule_of_three
patterns.description: Forcing everything into groups of three items, benefits, or points.
patterns.example_bad: Speed, efficiency, and reliability. Three key benefits. Three main features. Three steps.
patterns.fix: Use natural item counts. Sometimes two is enough. Sometimes you need four. Forced triples are a tell.

patterns.name: copula_avoidance
patterns.example_bad: The city boasts impressive architecture. The platform features robust analytics.
patterns.fix: The city has impressive architecture. The platform has analytics. Simple verbs are fine.

patterns.name: significance_inflation
patterns.description: Making ordinary things sound historically important with grandiose framing.
patterns.example_bad: A pivotal moment in the evolution of digital transformation...
patterns.fix: State the fact plainly. If it's actually significant, the details will show that.

patterns.name: negative_parallelism
patterns.description: 'It's not just X, it's Y' construction used for emphasis.
patterns.example_bad: It's not just a tool, it's a revolution.
patterns.fix: Just say what it is directly. The 'not just... it's' pattern is an AI crutch.

patterns.name: formulaic_challenge_dismiss
patterns.description: 'Despite challenges... continues to thrive' template that dismisses complexity.
patterns.example_bad: Despite facing numerous challenges, the company continues to thrive and innovate.
patterns.fix: Name the specific challenges and what actually happened. Don't hand-wave.

patterns.name: perfect_grammar
patterns.description: Zero fragments, zero starting with conjunctions, zero contractions throughout. Too clean.
patterns.example_bad: The system is effective. It provides value. Users appreciate the functionality.
patterns.fix: Use fragments. Start with 'And' or 'But'. Use contractions. Real writing has texture.

patterns.name: inline_header_lists
patterns.description: **Bold Label:** content format used everywhere instead of prose.
patterns.fix: Write in prose. It's fast, reliable, and scales. Headers are for major sections only.

patterns.name: title_case_everything
patterns.description: Using Title Case For Every Heading And Subheading.
patterns.fix: Use sentence case: 'Getting started with the platform'. Title case every word looks automated.
